chapter: WPA band and 1930s New Orleans bands
title: New Orleans men with Bob Crosby; Harry Shields
summary: Sal lists New Orleans players in the Bobcats and tells why Harry Shields kept quitting jobs, and his brother Eddie Shields.

story.theme_name: Who was in the band: naming sidemen and personnel
story.community_name: Who played in the band: reciting personnel

blocks.x: Didn't you tell me that there was a lot of New Orleans musicians with the March of the Bobcat with Bob Crosby? Oh, I didn't know that.

You told me about the Blackhawk. Yeah, I said the Blackhawk. Yeah, Napoli Lamar, Eddie Miller, Fize, who else now? Hilton Lamar, Eddie Miller. Raymond Padua. Ray Padua. Ray Padua. And so the bass player was Bobby Haggard up there. And then Shields, always putting a job. I mean, I can't knock Harry, man. And Harry could always play clarinet, always. I played with his brother too, Eddie. You mean Eddie Shields? I've heard of him, I never met him. He played piano band, Eddie. I played with Larry in the disc. My brother Larry, man. When was that you played with Larry? When he'd come back from the Dixie Land band, you know. When Harry was always quitting. When I got to see, man, I was always breaking much Harry Shields. I played with Larry, man.

Nothing he played in those days. He said, man, my brother played way better than I played. I didn't think so. I think Harry for me was good. He played with the piano band. He played with the piano band, Eddie. I played with Larry in the disc. My brother Larry, man. I think Harry Shields played with me. He plays good enough, man. I think he played with the piano band. He said, man, my brother played way better than I played. I didn't think so. I think Harry for me was great. That's right. That's one thing I can't say about Harry Shields. I knew when he couldn't play. I didn't. When I played with Harry Shields, he played great, man. He was so good he was always quitting jobs. He said, man, too hard, man. I didn't want that to be recorded either. I want to say it. I'll save it for Harry Shields. I'll save it for Harry Shields. What about Sam Majada? Did you ever work with him? Yeah, poor Sam. I had a picture with Sam if I could find him. Yeah. You have another phone in there with some pictures, don't you? I play with Sam Majada. I've seen that picture with the police guy. He's a guy. He's a guy.
